clue.text: Dressing-gown for Bob, with heart disorder

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shopping for a dressing-gown for Bob, who has a heart condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' looks like Bob's illness but is the anagram signal working on BOB and HEART together.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathrobe is a loose wrap worn over nightclothes, the same garment as a dressing-gown.

clue.text: Operation to avoid

explanation.surface: Someone describing surgery they want to dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart surgery that reroutes blood is a bypass, and to bypass something is to go round it and avoid it.

clue.text: Play patience

explanation.surface: An instruction to deal out a game of solitaire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' is a noun here: the slack or free movement in a mechanism, as in a wheel with a little play.
explanation.definitionFit: Engineers call the permitted slack in a part its allowance or play, and forbearance with others is a kind of patience.

clue.text: Effect upholstery repair for rally

explanation.surface: A note about reupholstering furniture in preparation for a rally.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it RE-COVER for the upholstery sense, and read it whole for regaining strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting new fabric on a sofa is covering it again, while to rally after illness is to regain health.

clue.text: Side shown by Bill, in good French environment

indicators.note: the French word forms the surroundings in which the bill sits

parts.note: bon is French for good
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A dish served with the bill in a nice French setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side' is a side of bacon, the flank of a pig cured whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a cured half-carcass of pork, the traditional cut sold as a flitch.

clue.text: Seductive centre of interest in relation to the ear

indicators.note: the middle two letters of the word interest are taken

parts.note: otic is the medical adjective for the ear

explanation.surface: Someone finds the ear a seductive focus of attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seductive arouses sexual desire, which is what the adjective for sensual love describes.

clue.text: Reappears with tickets for the round-trip

explanation.surface: Someone coming back with tickets for a journey there and back.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a return ticket is a round-trip ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who comes back reappears, and round-trip tickets are what British travellers call returns.

clue.text: Put up most healthy section of bone

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up means the letters are read from the bottom upward

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, in top condition; the figure 1 serves as the letter I
a bit is a section or piece

explanation.surface: A request to set out the healthiest part of a bone.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is read as AI; it and BIT together are turned upward to give the shinbone.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, the larger of the two lower leg bones.

clue.text: Scrutineers of draughts in America?

explanation.surface: A query about vote-counters of draughts in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for the board game Americans call checkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrutineers are people who inspect and verify, and in the US the game of draughts goes by another name.

clue.text: Daisy's conveyance following the divorce?

parts.note: the old song has Daisy on a bicycle built for two; once the couple split, only a one-wheeled, one-rider machine is left

explanation.surface: A wry question about how Daisy gets about after splitting up.
explanation.walkthrough: The music-hall song 'Daisy Bell' promises Daisy a 'bicycle built for two'.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-wheeled cycle is for one rider, the joke being that a divorced Daisy no longer needs a tandem.

clue.text: Bobby in a manner of speaking?

definitions.text: Bobby in a manner of speaking?

parts.words: Bobby in a manner of speaking?
parts.note: 'bobby' is a slang manner of speaking for a British police officer, so the formal title is what the slang means

explanation.surface: A remark that Bobby is only so in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bobby' looks like a name; it is British slang for a police officer, after Sir Robert Peel.
explanation.definitionFit: A bobby is the colloquial British word for a uniformed officer of the lowest police rank.

clue.text: Having absolved penitent from shilling rent

parts.note: SH is an abbreviation for the old shilling coin
rent, the past of rend, means torn apart, as does riven

explanation.surface: A priest who has pardoned a sinner from a shilling's rent.
explanation.walkthrough: The shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, abbreviated sh. 'rent' is not money here but the past tense of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrive is to hear confession and give absolution, so a priest who has absolved has done that.

clue.text: Fish with old craft a lot in America

parts.note: the carp is a freshwater fish
Noah's ark is an ancient vessel

explanation.surface: Someone with a fish and an old boat, and a lot of them in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' is a parking lot, the American term for this space.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call an area for leaving vehicles a parking lot; the British use a different two-word name.

clue.text: Revolutionary car-chain broken

indicators.note: a broken chain's letters come apart and are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A revolutionary-style car chain has snapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawless and rebellious, rejecting all order, as a revolutionary would.

clue.text: Chief stableman around the north makes a point

parts.note: a head is a chief or leader

indicators.note: the stable worker's word wraps round the letter for north

parts.note: a lad is a stable hand in British racing
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A head groom surrounding the north side makes a point in argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes a point' sounds like arguing, but the point is a promontory.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland is a promontory jutting into the sea, also called a point.

clue.text: Sunday outing to see the river

parts.note: a tour is a trip or outing

explanation.surface: A Sunday trip to visit the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stour is the name of several English rivers, notably in Dorset and in Suffolk.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stour is an English waterway, the name given to several rivers in southern and eastern England.

clue.text: Error in this Grove edition?

indicators.note: a new edition of the words recasts their letters in a different order

explanation.surface: A query about a mistake in this edition of Grove's music dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Grove is the standard dictionary of music, which runs to many editions.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversight is a slip or mistake made by failing to notice something.

clue.text: Waste in solid fuel is immense

indicators.note: the word for waste sits inside the word for solid fuel

parts.note: coal is a solid fuel
loss is wastage or waste

explanation.surface: A complaint that waste in solid fuel is enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal means vast or gigantic, like the huge statue of Rhodes.

clue.text: Work period of Falstaff, for example

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a numbered work
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Discussing the working period of Shakespeare's fat knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falstaff' looks like the Shakespeare character, but here it is Verdi's last stage work, named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's Falstaff is a sung stage drama with orchestra, one example of the form.

clue.text: Receives grants

explanation.surface: A bare statement of someone taking in grants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grants' is a verb here: concedes or admits.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes delivery of something receives it, and someone who concedes a point allows it.

clue.text: Statistics of people who have been in hailstorms?

definitions.text: Statistics of people who have been in hailstorms?

parts.words: Statistics of people who have been in hailstorms?
parts.note: the mean figures are statistics; split the word as 'ave' (hail, the Latin greeting) and 'rages' (storms), so hail-storms gives it whole

explanation.surface: A survey of people caught in bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: Ave is Latin for hail, a greeting, and rages are storms.
explanation.definitionFit: Means and medians are statistics summarising a set of figures, the typical value per person.

clue.text: Bridges, for example, not opening when covered in gold

indicators.note: the first letter of the title is removed, the opening of the word dropped

parts.note: Robert Bridges was Poet Laureate from 1913 to 1930

explanation.surface: Bridges, not opening, when coated in gold leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridges' looks like spans but is Robert Bridges, a British Poet Laureate; the title loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aureate means golden or gilded, from the Latin for gold.

clue.text: In cowboy's terms, he has very little to say

definitions.text: he has very little to say

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A remark that, in cowboy talk, a man is laconic.
explanation.walkthrough: The shellfish is proverbially silent: to be 'close as an oyster' is to keep quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: The bivalve is a byword for silence and secrecy, so a tight-lipped person is likened to it.

clue.text: Making light of Capitol disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves the building's letters in ruins, to be reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone playing down a catastrophe at the US Capitol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making light of' sounds like downplaying; the definition is 'light', and optical means relating to light.
explanation.definitionFit: Optical relates to sight and visible radiation, as in an optical microscope that uses light.

clue.text: Turkey on plate to consume as' special surprise

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another stands above it

parts.note: TR is the international code for Turkey
food on a plate is there to eat

explanation.surface: Turkey served on a plate as a special surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' looks like the bird but is the country, coded TR.
explanation.definitionFit: A treat is an unexpected delight or indulgence given as a special pleasure.

clue.text: Canon Henry is so lazy!

parts.note: a writer's canon is their body of works
Hy is a traditional abbreviation of the name Henry

explanation.surface: An exclamation that a churchman called Henry is idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canon' looks like a clergyman but is a writer's body of work; Hy. is an old written short form of Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone averse to labour and avoiding effort is idle, the meaning of lazy.

clue.text: Open up with'"Daybreak in Vienna'?

indicators.note: the dawn letter goes inside the city's German name

parts.note: Wien is the German name for Vienna
the break, or start, of day is its first letter

explanation.surface: Opening with a song or film titled Daybreak in Vienna.
explanation.walkthrough: Vienna is written in its own language, Wien, and the D that opens 'day' goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To widen is to make broader, opening something up.

clue.text: Narcotic, saline drug the GP ordered?

indicators.note: the letters are put in a fresh order, with a pun on a doctor ordering a medicine

explanation.surface: A doctor prescribing a saline-based drug for a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' reads as what the GP (British family doctor) prescribed, but it is the anagram signal on SALINE DRUG THE GP.
explanation.definitionFit: A dose taken to induce slumber is a narcotic, a drug that dulls the senses.

clue.text: Up to date news of city trial

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: Asking for the current news on a city's court case.
explanation.definitionFit: The most recent information is the newest news, what is current.

clue.text: South American native taking in colonial workers

parts.note: worker ants live in colonies
an eater is one who takes in food

explanation.surface: A South American local hiring colonial labourers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'colonial workers' sounds like empire labour; they are ants, and one 'taking them in' eats them.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant tamandua-like mammal of the Americas is a native creature with a long tongue for insects.
